Docket 1.3.80

**Fewer findings that were wrong about well-built sites.**

Since 1.3.79 Docket has been pointed at a set of well-known, well-built
websites, and every serious finding it made was checked by hand against the
pages themselves. These are the ones that turned out to be wrong, now fixed.

- *"No analytics tag on any page"* on sites that run privacy-focused analytics
  from their own domain, rather than from the vendor's. Docket only recognised
  the vendor-hosted form. Both self-hosted forms are now recognised.
- *A retired analytics tag reported as still loading* on a site that has never
  had it. A common browser-compatibility tag in the page's head was being read
  as an analytics ID. It no longer is.
- *Analytics "missing from every page"* on a site that loads all of its tags
  with JavaScript. When Docket renders a page and finds tags the plain page
  didn't show, it no longer reports a gap it cannot measure.
- *"Invisible to AI crawlers"* on pages that are simply short. A page with
  little text in a large file used to be assumed to be built by JavaScript.
  Docket now renders the pages it suspects, and a page that is short both
  before and after rendering is reported as short instead.
- *"Invisible to AI crawlers"* and *"almost no content"* on login and
  password-reset pages. Those are forms, not pages anyone should quote.
- *"Pages competing for the same search"* on archives: release notes and
  meeting minutes that differ only by a version or a date. Each one is its own
  record. The finding also now shows which pages are in each group, where
  before it only listed them.
- *"No identifiable logo"* on pages that name the business in their link back
  to the homepage without a logo image.
- *"Returned only the site navigation"* now says what it measures — mostly
  navigation — and names the other likely cause: a page with almost nothing on
  it.

99 checks across 13 areas.
